title: Ops-led cost tradeoff workbench for private deployments
summary: Working spreadsheet + operator playbook for comparing on-prem vs VPC private deployment TCO across licensing and support bundle mixes. Focus is on actionable ops levers and a compact scenario matrix for sales + SREs to run quick estimates.
body:
Purpose:
This is an ops-led workbench (working spreadsheet + notes) to: 1) surface the dominant cost levers for on-prem vs VPC private deployments; 2) enumerate support and licensing bundle breakpoints; and 3) provide a replicable scenario matrix and short checklist SRE/Ops can use during customer scoping calls.

Context and constraints:
- Audience: solutions engineering, product, SRE/ops, and pricing. Not a polished finance model — this is intentionally lightweight and prescriptive so field teams can run 3–4 scenarios in 10–20 minutes.
- Horizon: 3-year comparisons (year 0 purchase + years 1–2 ops).
- Scope: hardware amortization, infra ops headcount delta, datacenter T&M (power, cooling, network, racking), cloud VPC equivalent instance costs, reserved vs burst capacity, license & support fees, and residual software engineering integration/time-to-production.
- Excluded: customer-specific discounts and bespoke hardware financing terms (these are knobs to be added per-deal).

Quick instructions for using the sheet (tab names):
- Inputs: single-pane inputs where SEs enter customer profile (peak rps, avg tokens/session, SLO, region, preferred model family, on-call SLA).
- Capacity-calculator: derived GPU count for target p95 latency and concurrency assumptions. Include a small sensitivity table (quantization and batching gain multipliers).
- CapEx: HW list (GPU SKU, CPU, RAM, storage, NICs), rack spaces per cluster, freight/setup and installation. Fields: qty, unit cost, vendor lead time, useful life (months), depreciation schedule (straight-line).
- OpEx: power (kWh * price), cooling overhead (%), colo/network rent, patching/maintenance, spare parts budget.
- Headcount-delta: incremental FTEs for ops and SRE (on-call bounding, runbooks), estimated salary loaded cost per FTE, assumed utilization.
- Licensing+Support: license price bands (per-GPU or per-cluster), tiered support (standard, enterprise, premium) with response times and escalation hours. Options to model managed-support add-on (redwood-managed-onprem).
- VPC-equivalent: mapping of CapEx+OpEx into cloud instance types, egress assumptions, regional price multipliers, sustained use discounts/reservations, and burst vs reserved cost delta.
- Scenario-matrix: prefilled scenarios (Conservative on-prem, Aggressive on-prem, Small VPC, Large VPC) with 3-year NPV and payback.
- Recommendations: auto-generated text snippets that the SE can copy into proposals (based on scenario winners and risk notes).

Key formulas / levers to capture (written so non-sheet users can replicate quickly):
- GPU_count = ceil( (expected_tokens_per_sec * avg_token_cost_factor) / (tokens_per_gpu_per_sec * target_utilization) )
- Onprem_total_annualized = (CapEx_total / useful_life_years) + OpEx_annual + Headcount_costs_annual + Support_license_annual
- VPC_total_annualized = instance_hourly_cost * hours_per_year + egress_est + managed_service_fee + license_if_any
- 3yr_NPV = sum( annual_cashflow_t / (1 + discount_rate)^t ) for t=0..2; allow discount_rate input
- Break-even_months = CapEx_delta / monthly_cashflow_delta (for capex-heavy on-prem vs opex cloud)

Practical heuristics (operational):
- If peak utilization < 20% and unpredictable spiky traffic => VPC often favored.
- If steady-state utilization > 50% for baseline model family with predictable scheduling => on-prem may win after 12–18 months, depending on power/rack economics.
- Support bundles: incremental support cost becomes dominant when customer requires 24/7 escalation + on-site SLAs. Flag: enterprise-support premium > 15% of license is a strong signal to prefer managed dedicated.
- Ops friction: add a "time-to-first-serve" multiplier (weeks to onboard) which attaches a soft cost = lost revenue risk + SE time. Useful for early-stage startups without infra team.

Sample scenario outputs (example numbers — replace via Inputs):
- Customer: mid-market SaaS, EU region, target 1k concurrent sessions, 200 tokens/session avg, 99.9% p95 latency target
  - Capacity calc: baseline model => equivalent 8x A100-80GB nodes at 60% utilization (assumed).
  - On-prem CAPEX estimate: $1.6M HW + $80k installation + $120k spares (year0). Annualized over 3 yrs => $600k/year.
  - On-prem Opex: power & colo: $180k/year. Headcount delta: 1.5 FTE ops => $280k/year. Support/licensing: $150k/year. Total on-prem annualized ≈ $1.21M/year.
  - VPC estimate: reserved instances + moderate egress => $1.05M/year (including managed service margin).
  - Recommendation (toy): VPC preferred for year1 due to faster TTF and lower ops lift; if customer expects predictable growth and can commit to 3-year reservation with higher utilization (>60%), re-run model with reservation multiplier -> on-prem may become competitive in year2.

Decision checklist for SEs (quick copyable during calls):
1) What is 12-month expected avg utilization? (low/medium/high)
2) Do you require on-site support or local data residency that prevents cloud in region X?
3) Expected growth profile (bursty vs linear).
4) Does customer have existing colo contracts or hardware relationships?
5) Are there procurement constraints that mandate CapEx vs Opex preferences?
6) Acceptable time-to-ship/handover (lead times for hardware > 8 weeks push toward VPC).
7) Security/KMS constraints for private keys (if strict, treat as compliance delta and add managed-service premium).

Open questions / TODOs for follow-up (internal):
- Validate vendor list and up-to-date per-GPU street prices for EMEA and APAC (Priya).
- Add a column to model "quantization/compilation" uplift (we currently use a 1.3x perf multiplier default) and allow quick toggle to 1.6x for LLMs that support int8/fp8.
- Establish recommended default support bundle mapping (standard => 8% of license, enterprise => 18%, premium => 30%) and source historical deal wins where deviation occurred.
- Add a short script (python) that converts the sheet output to a one-page PDF with scenario highlights and recommended next steps (Jonah).

Risks and notes to pricing/legal:
- This model intentionally excludes partner discounts and financing deals; include an override field for final quote.
- On-prem meter: warranty and spare part SLAs are often the hidden cost. We recommend conservative spare budget of 5–8% of HW list price/year.

Appendix: quick macros / snippets to copy into proposals
- "Recommendation: For customers with <20% expected baseline utilization and spiky traffic, Redwood recommends VPC private deployment for year 1 to minimize ops lift and accelerate time-to-value. If you plan to sustain >50% utilization for 24+ months, consider on-prem with a 3-year reservation and enterprise support."
footer: Draft internal workbench — do not share externally without PR/Legal review.
